items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I did get a chance to go on the road with this guy Buddy Miles.

ctx.x: Okay. When I was in music school there was a group of us that were so intent on — we used the term “making it.” We wanted to make it in the music business. And I’m not even sure we knew what it meant but I’m curious if you had that same feeling when you were young, and did you have an idea of what it meant to be successful or to make it?

I did, and on the other side of the coin I really didn’t. But the first time somebody paid me to play the trumpet I got into, when I got into high school I came into the high school jazz band from junior high, and the band director at the high school — and the band director of the junior high school was my first trumpet teacher. He was a very good player and I studied with him through high school. And he told the high school band director, “Hey I’ve got your lead trumpet player coming,” you know, “this kid can…

bucks and we’d play weddings on the weekends. So now all of a sudden I’m doing a couple of gigs and making 150 bucks on the weekends in the 70s. And I was like, man, I’ve made it, man. I never flipped burgers, or I never did any of that. Now I did do some other day jobs. I worked as a machinist because my father was a machinist. So the day jobs I took were those things. Then as I started playing I kind of made some money, you know, through high school, and I got to where I could drive eventually and of course…
